entities.name: PMID:27490331
observations: Jilg et al. studied male wild-type and MT1/Mel1a-deficient mice for feeding behavior and Pomc/Npy expression in the arcuate nucleus and pituitary.
MT1/Mel1a deficiency increased time spent feeding without changing total food intake, body weight, or general locomotor behavior.
Nocturnal Pomc expression was lower in the arcuate nucleus and pituitary pars distalis of MT1-deficient mice; pars intermedia Pomc showed no genotype difference.
Light-phase melatonin increased Pomc expression in wild-type but not MT1-deficient mice, supporting MT1-dependent stimulation.

entities.name: MTNR1A
observations: Loss of MTNR1A/MT1/Mel1a signaling in mice altered feeding duration and reduced nocturnal Pomc expression in the arcuate nucleus and pituitary pars distalis.

entities.name: POMC
observations: In MTNR1A-deficient mice, nocturnal Pomc mRNA was reduced in arcuate nucleus and pituitary pars distalis but unchanged in pars intermedia.
Melatonin stimulated Pomc expression in wild-type but not MTNR1A-deficient mice.

entities.name: Altered feeding dynamics
observations: MT1/Mel1a-deficient mice spent more time feeding than wild-type mice, without increased total food consumption.
